tldr: On Oct 1, Anthropic's Claude Code team published a guide to mods: hooks that ship inside plugins and run within a Claude Code session. The guide builds one from an empty folder, then tours two larger mods.
whats_new: Digitimes (Oct 5) frames DeepSeek Harness's Claude Code mods bridge and open plugin architecture as a challenge to agent lock-in, following the Oct 4 v0.2.1-alpha.1 compatibility layer.
why_it_matters: Mods are a plugin-level extension point, so a second agent runtime accepting the same format lowers the cost of moving mod-based workflows between harnesses.

status.detail: Claude Code mods have an official guide, an experimental DeepSeek Harness compatibility layer, and now trade-press framing as an anti-lock-in move.

beats.headline: Claude Code mods guide: hooks shipped inside plugins
beats.summary: Walks through building a mod from an empty folder and two larger examples.

beats.headline: DeepSeek Harness adds an experimental mods compatibility layer
beats.summary: Alpha release, DeepSeek rejecting the "copying homework" charge, and a Digitimes read of it as an open-plugin challenge to lock-in.

open_questions: Does the Harness compatibility layer run existing Claude Code mods unmodified, or only a subset of hooks?
Will Anthropic document mods as a stable cross-runtime format, or keep them Claude Code specific?
take_for_builders: If you build Claude Code mods, keep hook logic free of Claude-specific paths for now; test against the Harness alpha only on throwaway projects until its coverage is documented.
